title: Export Tutorial
subtitle: A complete guide to exporting SDG analysis results in multiple formats
about_body: This tutorial walks you through exporting SDG analysis results into multiple formats such as PDF, CSV, Excel, and JSON. Exports let you save, share, and integrate research results with other systems.

steps.title: Finish the Analysis
steps.description: Make sure you've finished the SDG analysis for the article or researcher profile.

steps.title: Click Export
steps.description: On the results page, click the 'Export Results' button in the top-right corner.

steps.title: Pick a Format
steps.description: Choose the export format that fits your needs (PDF, CSV, Excel, or JSON).

steps.title: Download & Share
steps.description: The file downloads automatically. You can save it or share it with colleagues.

formats.title: PDF Document
formats.description: Portable document format, ideal for official reports, presentations, and archives.

formats.title: CSV Data
formats.description: Raw data format that opens in any spreadsheet application.
formats.useCase: Advanced data analysis, import into stats tools

formats.title: Excel Spreadsheet
formats.description: Spreadsheet format with formatting and multi-sheet support.
formats.useCase: Deep analysis, pivot tables, data visualization

formats.title: JSON Data
formats.description: Structured data format for API integration and application development.

data_items: Give files descriptive names that include the analysis date
Keep backups in cloud storage for safety
collab_items: PDF is ideal for stakeholder distribution
JSON is best for integrating with other systems

issues.solution: Check your browser settings for pop-up blockers and download permissions.
Make sure every part of the analysis has loaded before exporting.
Try an alternate format, or update your browser to the latest version.

cta_body: Run an SDG analysis now and export the results in multiple formats for your research and reporting needs
